title: Confession and Repentance
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Confession and repentance are the believer’s honest admission of sin before God and turning from sin back to Him. They are not attempts to earn forgiveness, but responses of faith to God’s grace and truth.
summary: Confession and repentance are the believer’s honest admission of sin before God and turning from sin back to Him. They are not attempts to earn forgiveness, but responses of faith to God’s grace and truth.
christFocus: Jesus Christ provides forgiveness and cleansing for those who confess their sins. His mercy allows believers to come into the light instead of hiding in shame or self-defense.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Believers still need confession and repentance. To claim sinlessness is self-deception. God calls His people to come honestly into the light, naming sin without hiding, excusing, or minimizing it.

Confession is not mere regret over consequences. It is agreement with God about sin. Repentance turns from sin toward God with humility, faith, and desire for restored obedience.

The promise of cleansing rests on God’s faithfulness and justice in Christ. Believers confess not to persuade God to become merciful, but because mercy has been opened through Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Hidden sin hardens the heart and weakens fellowship with God. Shame often drives people into secrecy, while pride drives them into excuses. Confession and repentance break both patterns.

This doctrine gives hope for returning to God. The way back is not pretending, blaming, or despairing, but honest confession before the faithful Savior.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess sin quickly and specifically before God. Do not protect darkness with excuses. Turn from what God exposes, receive His forgiveness in Christ, and seek wise help where patterns of sin need accountability, repair, or restoration.
